frontend/apps/mobile/src/hooks/useApi.ts:82-91 — the central `apiRequest` helper throws on any non-ok response (including 401) with a plain `Error(message)`; no branch attempts a refresh_token exchange and no 401 handler retries the original request. Every useQuery/useMutation across the mobile app will therefore surface a fresh 'Unauthorized' error the moment the short-lived access token expires, forcing manual re-login even when the refresh token is still valid.
verified in-run 2026-08-03: read apiRequest at :76-91 — sole failure branch throws; no interceptor / no 401 retry path exists in the file

frontend/apps/mobile/src/nfc/NFCAccessController.ts:274 — `if (new Date(credential.validUntil) < now)` where `now = new Date()` uses the local device clock. On any device where the user can adjust the system time (default on Android/iOS with no MDM lock), an expired credential is accepted as valid — physical-access bypass with no signal recorded server-side.
verified in-run 2026-08-03: read validateAccess :249-290 — expiry check is client-side date-comparison against device clock with no server-issued freshness proof or nonce.
Vector escalated to `security` (was `bug` in dispatcher tier1d): a credential-expiry bypass on a physical-access system is confidentiality/integrity risk, not just a functional defect.

frontend/apps/mobile/src/nfc/NFCAccessController.ts (478 lines) and nfc/NFCCredentialManager.ts (321 lines) have ZERO test files. NFC access is a physical-security-adjacent module (deny/grant on credentials) so shipping without unit-tested access decisions is a coverage gap that will bite on any refactor.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/hooks/usePerformanceMetrics.ts:160-164 — the effect cleanup ONLY disconnects the PerformanceObserver but never removes the window `visibilitychange` and `load` listeners that were registered earlier in the same effect. Every remount/unmount cycle leaks two more listeners; over the lifetime of an SPA session that means N growing subscribers all firing on each visibility change.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/portfolio-performance/pages/PortfolioDashboardPage.tsx — the entire shipped manager-facing portfolio dashboard renders `mockDashboardSummary` and `mockPropertyCards` constants defined in the file; there is no API call, no useQuery, no props from a real fetch. Every manager viewing 'their' portfolio sees the identical fake `Downtown Office Building / 123 Main St` values regardless of tenant.

verified in-run 2026-08-03: read PortfolioDashboardPage.tsx :1-50 — component body imports React + card components then binds hardcoded `mockDashboardSummary` object literal (totalPortfolioValue 2_500_000 EUR, etc.). Comment on line 17 says 'would be fetched from API'.

frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/compliance/pages/ContentModerationPage.tsx:130-146 — free-form window.prompt() text is `as`-cast into an enum-typed action parameter without runtime validation, so any operator typing 'nuke' will send an invalid moderation action to the API. Native prompt() also breaks the moderator flow on mobile/native shells that suppress it.

Numerous user-facing browser-dialog strings across ppt-web are hardcoded English instead of going through react-i18next `t(...)`, even in translated-elsewhere features. Same class as reality-web i18n gap: sk/cs users see raw English in confirms/prompts.
